findings.comment: Austin Energy Standard Notes block is not identified on the Cover Sheet (Sheet 1), General Notes (Sheet 3), or Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21). Typical AE Standard Notes should include clearance requirements, easement access, tree work responsibilities, transmission safety requirements, and meter installation standards per UCM § 1.16.0. Verify if AE standard notes have been provided and add them to the plans if not present.

A note stating that all electric infrastructure (new and existing) is shown on the plans and that exceptions requiring Austin Energy pre-approval are not present is not clearly evident on the submitted sheets. Add explicit note per UCM § 1.16.0(1) stating: 'All electric infrastructure is shown. Any exceptions to standard service require Austin Energy Design approval.'

Electrical site plan lacks critical coordination measurements and details required for Austin Energy Design approval. Missing: 20' × 35' setup area dimensions in front of transformer access doors with 35-foot vertical clearance; clearance measurements from proposed facilities to property lines and existing structures; transformer disconnect location and meter-to-disconnect distance (maximum 20 feet); truck access path dimensions (12-foot horizontal width, 16-foot vertical clearance); bollard and curb details for protection of equipment; and staging area notes. Add detailed coordination measurements and setup area annotations per UCM § 1.16.0(2) and § 1.3.16.

Electrical easements are not explicitly distinguished between aerial (accommodating overhead poles, conductors, and guy wires with vertical clearance requirements) and non-aerial/underground (accommodating subsurface conduit, pad-mounted transformers, and underground laterals). Existing easements labeled only as generic 'Public Utility Easements' or '5' Electric Easement' without designation as aerial vs. underground. Clarify each electric easement label to specify whether it is designated for aerial or underground facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i).

applicableAreas: Electrical easements on site plan (Sheet 9) and electrical design plan (Sheet 21)
findings.comment: While two 5-foot electric easements from the Mecey Subdivision plat are visible on sheets 9 and 21 with partial recording references (Vol. 73, Pg. 76 and Vol. 5468, Pg. 883), complete recording information (document number/instrument number and exact volume/page citations matching the recorded instruments) is not consistently provided on all plan sheets. Add complete recording information including instrument number, volume number, page number, and filing date for all existing electric easements per UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i).

Electric easements (5' easements noted on existing recorded plat) are labeled on the plans with partial identifying information but do not include dimension callouts showing the exact width and linear extent of each easement. Add dimension annotations to all electric easement boundaries showing the width (e.g., 5') and the length/extent of each easement along the property boundary per UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i).

Electric facilities are not shown consistently on all required plan sheets. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows transformers and meters, but the Grading Plan (Sheet 11) does not explicitly show or reference the transformer locations and electrical conduit routing. The Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) references overhead electric in the legend but does not consistently show electrical infrastructure relative to planting and tree locations. Electrical facilities must be shown on site plan (9), utility plan (21), landscape plan (31), grading plan (11), and where relevant, erosion control, irrigation, and storm sewer plan sheets per UCM § 1.16.0(1).

applicableAreas: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan)
findings.comment: Transformer symbols appear to be labeled differently across sheets. Sheet 9 references 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' while Sheet 21 shows 'Electrical Transformer Pad'. Verify that all electrical equipment symbols (transformers, meters, pull boxes, distribution equipment) are depicted using consistent symbols and labels throughout all plan sheets where electrical infrastructure appears.

While transformer pad locations appear to be consistent between Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan), the Grading Plan (Sheet 11) does not clearly show these transformer locations, making it impossible to verify cross-sheet consistency of electrical facility locations relative to grades, contours, and site elevations. Ensure electrical facility locations (transformers, meters, service points, conduits) match exactly across all plan sheets by adding electrical symbols/callouts to the grading plan where relevant per UCM § 1.16.0(1).

applicableAreas: Landscape plan (Sheet 31), Electrical design plan (Sheet 21), Site plan (Sheet 9)
findings.comment: Tree locations shown on the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) and Existing Tree Plan (Sheet 30) are not coordinated with electrical infrastructure shown on Sheets 9, 21, and landscape plan regarding clearance requirements. No notes confirm that landscaping avoids 15-foot radial clearance zones from overhead distribution conductors, 7.5-foot horizontal clearance from overhead conductors, 20'×35' setup areas for transformer access, or appropriate clearances from utility pole guy anchors. Verify coordination between landscape design and existing/proposed electrical facilities per UCM § 1.16.0(1) and § 1.10.3, and add coordination notes where conflicts are resolved.

Sheet 21 references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' indicating that electrical utility profile information may be shown elsewhere. However, the Utility Tap Plan Profile (Sheet 20) focuses on water and wastewater lines. No profile sheets clearly showing existing utility poles with cross-arm widths (~8 feet) and depictions of NESC/OSHA clearance envelopes for overhead electrical facilities have been identified. Verify whether electrical utility profile sheets exist showing existing poles with clearance envelopes or provide them if required per UCM § 1.10.3.

applicableAreas: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) relative to transformer locations on Sheets 9 and 21
findings.comment: Three pad-mounted transformers are located in landscape islands within parking areas. The Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) does not indicate whether landscaping (trees, shrubs, irrigation, mulch) has been removed from the required 20' × 35' minimum setup area in front of transformer access doors or the 35-foot vertical clearance zone above transformers. The plan shows general landscape details but does not confirm clearance of these critical access and maintenance zones per UCM § 1.3.16. Annotate the landscape plan to show the 20' × 35' clear zone in front of each transformer as a 'no landscaping' area, or revise landscape design to provide adequate clearance.

Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' with the engineer's seal from Jason K. Rodgers (P.E.). No evidence indicates whether a licensed MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) consultant was engaged for this project or whether the electrical design meets the level of detail expected for a major project. Clarify whether this preliminary design has been or will be completed by an MEP professional and that final electrical design reflects current Austin Energy Design approval per reviewer convention for major projects.

Sheet 21 is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and contains electrical infrastructure (transformers, conduits, pull boxes, meters). However, it is not clear whether this sheet is organized exclusively for electric utilities or whether other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain, gas) are also shown on the same sheet. If electric and other utilities are combined on a single sheet, the sheet should be clearly labeled 'Electric Only' or clearly separated into utility-specific zones per reviewer convention for AE design criteria.

applicableAreas: General notes (Sheet 3) and electrical notes on various sheets
findings.comment: Review all plan notes to ensure no inapplicable or outdated electric infrastructure notes are included. Specifically verify that notes regarding EV charging, special electrical systems, network area vaults, or other facilities not proposed in the current Valley View Townhomes project are not present. If found, remove or update notes to reflect only applicable requirements per reviewer convention.

Plans do not explicitly demonstrate compliance with NESC (National Electrical Safety Code) requirements. While utility notes reference conductor verification and clearance requirements, specific NESC compliance statements, clearance verification data, or references to NESC standards are not prominently documented. Add note stating that electrical design, installation, and clearances comply with National Electrical Safety Code (NESC) per LDC § 25-4-200.

Plans do not explicitly demonstrate compliance with NEC (National Electrical Code) requirements. While the preliminary electrical design shows infrastructure layout, specific NEC compliance statements or references to NEC standards are not documented on the submitted sheets. Add note stating that electrical design, installation, and building electrical systems comply with National Electrical Code (NEC) per LDC § 25-4-200.

applicableAreas: All electrical design and coordination sheets
findings.comment: Plans do not contain an explicit compliance statement referencing UCM § 1.3.0 (Basic Requirements of Electric Distribution Service), § 1.3.3 (One Point of Service), § 1.3.8 (Property Line Crossings), § 1.3.12 (Line Extension Policy), § 1.9.3 (Metering), and Chapter 15-9 (Utility Service Regulations). While individual requirements may be addressed in plan notes and preliminary design, a comprehensive statement confirming compliance with all applicable UCM and City Code provisions is not evident. Add compliance note referencing applicable UCM sections and City Code Chapter 15-9 per LDC § 25-4-200.

Plans do not demonstrate that adequate access is preserved for Austin Energy personnel to maintain and service electrical facilities. Specifically: (1) The 20' × 35' setup areas in front of transformer access doors are not clearly delineated as requiring 35-foot vertical clearance and unrestricted ground access; (2) Truck access paths with minimum 12-foot horizontal and 16-foot vertical clearance capable of supporting 72,180 lbs vehicle weight are not annotated; (3) Access to existing utility poles and OHE infrastructure is not confirmed to be maintained. Add detailed truck access path dimensions, setup area clearance callouts, and confirmation that AE personnel can access all existing and proposed facilities for maintenance per UCM § 1.16.0(4).

Projected electrical load for the proposed development is not shown on the preliminary electrical design plan or any coordination documents. Sheet 21 shows transformer locations and equipment but does not include the total estimated electrical demand or individual building loads required for service design. Add the projected electrical load (demand) for the 39-unit townhome development in appropriate units (kVA, amps, or watts) on the electrical design plan and/or cover sheet per UCM § 1.16.0(6).

It is not clear whether Austin Energy Design has required a proximity survey documenting clearances from customer electrical facilities (service laterals, metering equipment, building systems) to existing AE primary voltage overhead conductors (12.47 kV distribution). Given that existing OHE facilities are present along the property boundaries (west and east sides), such a survey may be required. Verify with Austin Energy Design whether a clearance survey has been requested and, if so, provide it as part of the final electrical design per UCM § 1.10.3.

applicableAreas: Property boundaries relative to existing OHE facilities
findings.comment: Existing overhead electric (OHE) infrastructure is shown on property boundaries (west side along Valley View Road and east side), indicating that the subdivision/development site is within the 200-foot proximity trigger of existing Austin Energy infrastructure per LDC § 25-4-200(B). Verify that this 200-foot proximity condition has been identified and that appropriate Austin Energy approval and compliance demonstration has been obtained and documented in the site plan approvals or coordination documents.
